mainTopic: Where the מזוזה goes on a doorway, and which doorways and structures need one
overview: The גמרא explains שמואל's phrase 'the beginning of the upper third'. It means the מזוזה may not be lower than a third of the way down from the top beam. רבא says the מזוזה belongs in the outer טפח, nearest the street. One reason is so you meet it right away. Another is so it guards the whole house, and רבי חנינא adds that הקדוש ברוך הוא guards His servants from outside. רבא also rules that a מזוזה sunk a טפח deep is פסולה. A ברייתא suggested as support turns out to be about a second entrance behind the door. A reed doorframe must be set up before the מזוזה is placed in it, because of תעשה ולא מן העשוי. The גמרא then sorts out which structures need a מזוזה: broken entrances and a plain אכסדרה are פטור, a Roman portico is חייב, and a בי הרזיקי needs two. Finally, two pairs of אמוראים explain the dispute between רבי יוסי and חכמים about a gatehouse opening to a garden and a small room, and the second explanation finishes on the next amud.

steps.title: What did שמואל mean by 'the beginning of the upper third'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what שמואל's phrase 'the beginning of the upper third' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the meaning of 'the beginning of the upper third' that שמואל said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a phrase שמואל used earlier about how high to put the מזוזה and asks what it means. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'The beginning of the upper third' could sound like it tells you exactly where to place the מזוזה. The גמרא wants to know whether it is an exact spot or a limit.

keyTerms.meaning: The upper third (of the doorway's height)

phrases.english: And what is 'the beginning of the upper third'
phrases.notes: This is a phrase שמואל used just before this, about how high the מזוזה goes.

phrases.english: that he said?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי תְּחִילַּת שְׁלִישׁ הָעֶלְיוֹן דְּקָא אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of שמואל's ruling on the height of the מזוזה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the phrase 'the beginning of the upper third'.

steps.title: It is the farthest limit from the top beam
steps.stepSummary: The phrase sets a limit: the מזוזה may not be lower than a third of the way down from the top beam.
steps.simpleTranslation: It refers to how far you may distance it: you should not place it farther from the top beam than one third of the doorway's height.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that שמואל was giving the lowest point allowed for the מזוזה, not one exact spot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'The beginning of the upper third' is where the top third ends as you go down. So the מזוזה can be anywhere in the top third, but not below it.

keyTerms.meaning: To distance it (how far away it may go)
Beam, the top beam over the doorway

steps.whatToRemember: The upper third of the doorway is the zone for the מזוזה. It must not go lower than one third down from the top beam.

phrases.english: It refers to distancing it
(that one should not distance it from the beam
phrases.notes: Some versions have the words in round brackets and some don't.

phrases.english: above more than a third).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שמואל's phrase marks the lowest point allowed: no more than a third of the doorway's height below the top beam.

steps.title: Put the מזוזה in the outer handbreadth, near the street
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that the best place for the מזוזה is the טפח of the doorpost closest to the public domain.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא says: It is a מצוה to place the מזוזה in the handbreadth closest to the public domain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from רבא about where the מזוזה goes across the depth of the doorway, meaning toward the outside or the inside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 1 and 2 dealt with height. רבא adds a second direction: the doorpost has thickness, and the מזוזה should be on its outer edge, facing the street.

keyTerms.meaning: The preferred way to do it, a commandment

phrases.english: רבא says:
It is a מצוה to place it
in the handbreadth adjacent to the public domain.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מִצְוָה לְהַנִּיחָהּ בְּטֶפַח הַסָּמוּךְ לִרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: placement toward the outside, after the discussion of height.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מזוזה is ideally placed in the outermost טפח of the doorway, the one next to the public domain.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is why a מזוזה is put on the outer part of the doorpost and not deep inside the doorway.

steps.title: Why the outer handbreadth?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רבא's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the מזוזה should be on the side closest to the street. This sets up two different answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא gave the rule but no reason. The reason matters, because each reason shows a different purpose of the מזוזה.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason for רבא's ruling in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the מזוזה belongs in the טפח nearest the public domain.

steps.title: So you meet the מזוזה right away
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן explain that a person entering should meet the מצוה immediately.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן say: So that a person will meet the מזוזה immediately.
steps.whatsHappening: The first answer: if the מזוזה is on the outer edge, the moment you step into the doorway you are already at it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This reason is about the person: you should come across the מצוה at once and not walk partway in first. If the מזוזה were deeper in the doorway, you would reach it later.

keyTerms.meaning: That he will encounter or meet

phrases.english: The Rabbis say:
so that one encounters the mezuza immediately.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּנַן אָמְרִי: כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּפְגַּע בַּמְּזוּזָה מִיָּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The purpose is that a person meets the מצוה the moment he enters.

steps.title: So the מזוזה guards the whole house
steps.stepSummary: רב חנינא מסורא gives another reason: placing it outermost lets the מזוזה protect the house.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנינא from סורא says: So that it will guard it.
steps.whatsHappening: The second answer: placing the מזוזה at the outer edge lets it protect the entire house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This reason is about protection, not about meeting the מצוה. A guard stands at the outermost point so that everything inside is behind him. That leads straight into the next step.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥanina from Sura says:
so that it guards it.
phrases.notes: He means the מזוזה protects the house, and being at the outermost edge puts the whole house inside its guard.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חֲנִינָא מִסּוּרָא אוֹמֵר: כִּי הֵיכִי דְּתִינְטְרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, different answer to the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The purpose is protection: the outermost spot lets the מזוזה guard the whole house.

steps.title: A human king is guarded from outside, but ה׳ guards us from outside
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא contrasts human kings, who are guarded by their people, with הקדוש ברוך הוא, who guards His servants from outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא says: Come and see that the way of flesh and blood is not like the way of הקדוש ברוך הוא. With flesh and blood, the king sits inside and the people guard him from outside. With הקדוש ברוך הוא it is not so: His servants sit inside, and He guards them from outside, as it says: 'ה׳ is your guardian, ה׳ is your shade at your right hand.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds an אגדה that builds on the idea that the מזוזה guards the house. Through the מזוזה at the door, ה׳ stands outside guarding the Jew inside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With people, the important one is inside and the guards are outside. With ה׳ it is turned around: the King Himself stands guard outside for His servants. The פסוק of 'שומרך' backs this up.

keyTerms.meaning: The way of human beings, flesh and blood
The Holy One, Blessed be He

steps.whatToRemember: The מזוזה at the outer edge is a sign that ה׳ Himself stands guard at the door of the Jewish home.
steps.whyThisMatters: It gives a deeper meaning to רב חנינא מסורא's reason that the מזוזה guards the house.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥanina says:

phrases.aramaic: בּוֹא וּרְאֵה שֶׁלֹּא כְּמִדַּת הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
phrases.english: Come and see that not like the attribute of the Holy One, Blessed be He,
is the attribute of flesh and blood.
The attribute of flesh and blood:
a king sits inside,
and the people guard him from outside.

phrases.aramaic: מִדַּת הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אֵינוֹ כֵּן,
phrases.english: The attribute of the Holy One, Blessed be He, is not so:
His servants sit inside,
and He guards them from outside,
as it is stated:

phrases.aramaic: ״ה׳ שׁוֹמְרֶךָ ה׳ צִלְּךָ עַל יַד יְמִינֶךָ״.
phrases.english: "The Lord is your keeper, the Lord is your shade upon your right hand."

steps.triggerLanguage: בּוֹא וּרְאֵה שֶׁלֹּא כְּמִדַּת הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מִדַּת בָּשָׂר וְדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 6's idea that the מזוזה guards the house.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Unlike a human king, הקדוש ברוך הוא guards His servants from outside, and the מזוזה at the door shows this.

steps.title: A מזוזה sunk a handbreadth deep is invalid
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף son of רבא teaches in רבא's name that a מזוזה set a טפח deep into the doorpost is פסולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף son of רבא taught in the name of רבא: If one dug a טפח deep into the doorpost for the מזוזה, it is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ruling about depth: if you carve a hole a full טפח deep into the doorpost and put the מזוזה inside it, it does not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 1 and 3 dealt with height and with the outer edge. This adds a third limit: the מזוזה cannot be buried a טפח deep inside the post. רבא gives the ruling without a reason.

keyTerms.meaning: Invalid, does not fulfill the מצוה

phrases.english: Rav Yosef, son of Rava, taught
in the name of Rava:
If one dug a handbreadth deep for it,
phrases.notes: He means carving a hole into the doorpost and putting the מזוזה inside it.

phrases.english: it is unfit.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרֵשׁ רַב יוֹסֵף בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling, now about how deep into the doorpost the מזוזה may be placed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מזוזה sunk a טפח deep into the doorpost is פסולה.

steps.title: A ברייתא that may support רבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that a ברייתא about a מזוזה deep in the doorpost, or covered by an added frame, supports רבא's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say a ברייתא supports him? If one placed the מזוזה in the doorpost, or later added a frame over it, then if there is a טפח there, one needs another מזוזה. If not, one does not need another מזוזה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to agree with רבא: when the מזוזה ends up a טפח deep, you need a new one. The word 'לימא' (shall we say) warns that this proof may be questioned next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא has two cases: the מזוזה was set deep in the post, or a frame was added that covers it. In both, a depth of a טפח means the old מזוזה no longer counts, which matches רבא's rule that a טפח deep is פסולה.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say it supports him? (often a proof that may be rejected)
A frame added along the doorway

steps.confusionAlert: 'לימא' only suggests a proof. Don't assume the proof stands yet. The גמרא often goes on to push it away.

phrases.english: Let us say that this supports him:
If one placed it in the doorpost,
or added a frame onto it,
phrases.notes: He means a frame added to the doorway after the מזוזה was put up, so the מזוזה is now covered and set back.

phrases.english: if there is a handbreadth there,
one requires another mezuza;
if not,
one does not require another mezuza.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to support step 8's ruling from a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's ruling that a מזוזה sunk a טפח deep is פסולה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: if the מזוזה is in the doorpost or covered by an added frame, and there is a טפח there, another מזוזה is needed.

steps.title: The ברייתא may be about a second entrance behind the door
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof for רבא. It says the ברייתא about a טפח of depth is talking about a separate entrance behind the door, not a sunken מזוזה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When that ברייתא was taught, it was talking about an entrance that is behind the door.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from step 9. It reads the ברייתא as talking about a different case, so it does not support רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 9 the ברייתא seemed to say a מזוזה set a טפח deep is a problem, just like רבא said. Now the גמרא says the ברייתא means something else: when the doorframe is a טפח thick, the far side counts as its own entrance and needs its own מזוזה. That has nothing to do with a מזוזה becoming פסולה.

keyTerms.meaning: An entrance behind the door, on the other side of the same frame

phrases.english: When that [baraita] was taught,
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא brought as a proof for רבא in the last step.

phrases.english: it was about an entrance that is behind the door.
phrases.notes: Picture a thick frame with an opening on each side. The second opening counts as its own doorway.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof offered in step 9 by reading the ברייתא as a different case
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. רבא's ruling itself is not refuted.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא can be read as being about a second entrance, not about a sunken מזוזה.

steps.title: But the ברייתא states the behind-the-door case on its own
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rejection. The ברייתא openly mentions the case of an entrance behind the door as a separate line, so the earlier line must be about something else.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the ברייתא teaches that case openly: an entrance behind the door, if there is a טפח there, needs another מזוזה; and if not, it does not need another מזוזה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the rejection from step 10. If the ברייתא spells out the behind-the-door case separately, then the earlier line about depth must be a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא does not usually say the same thing twice. Since it lists the behind-the-door entrance as its own case, the earlier line about a טפח of depth seems to be about something else. That would bring back the proof for רבא.

phrases.english: But it teaches it openly:
an entrance that is behind the door,
if there is a handbreadth there,
it needs another mezuza;
and if not,
it does not need another mezuza!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rejection in step 10
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading in step 10 that the ברייתא's depth case is the behind-the-door entrance
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא states the behind-the-door case separately. If the first line were the same case, the ברייתא would be repeating itself.

steps.title: The later line explains which case the earlier line meant
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is not giving two rulings. The later line explains the earlier one: 'In what case? An entrance behind the door.'
steps.simpleTranslation: It is teaching 'how': it is explaining in what case the earlier ruling applies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge in two short words. The line about the entrance behind the door is not a new ruling; it explains the line before it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read the ברייתא as one ruling followed by its explanation: 'If there is a טפח, another מזוזה is needed. In what case? An entrance behind the door.' With that reading there is no repetition. The rejection from step 10 stands, and the ברייתא no longer proves רבא's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is teaching how', meaning the line explains the case of the line before it

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read the two lines of the ברייתא as two separate rulings. The second line just tells you which case the first line is about.

phrases.english: It is teaching "how" [in which case].
phrases.notes: In other words, the second line answers 'In what case did we say this?'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 11 and keeps the rejection from step 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the structure of the ברייתא: the later clause explains the earlier one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא lists two separate cases, so the depth clause must be about a sunken מזוזה
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא has one ruling plus its explanation, and both lines are about the entrance behind the door

steps.title: Putting a מזוזה in a frame made of reeds
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that for a doorframe made of reeds, one cuts a hollow tube in the reed and places the מזוזה inside it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: if one set up a frame of reeds for it, he cuts a tube and places the מזוזה in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: how to put up a מזוזה when the doorframe is made of reeds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reeds are hollow and you cannot nail into them well. So the ברייתא says to cut open a tube in the reed and set the מזוזה inside. The next step will add a condition to this.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנָא: הֶעֱמִיד לָהּ מַלְבֵּן שֶׁל קָנִים,
phrases.english: It was taught: If one set up a frame of reeds for it,
he cuts a tube and places it [the mezuza inside].

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: הֶעֱמִיד לָהּ מַלְבֵּן שֶׁל קָנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic about how to attach a מזוזה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a reed frame, one cuts a tube in the reed and places the מזוזה in it.

steps.title: The frame must be set up before the tube is cut
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא limits the ברייתא. It works only if the frame was put in place first and the tube cut afterward. If the מזוזה was placed first, it is פסולה because of תעשה ולא מן העשוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רבא said: They taught this only when he first set up the frame and afterward cut the tube and placed the מזוזה. But if he cut the tube and placed the מזוזה, and only afterward set up the frame, it is פסולה, because it says 'you shall make' and not from what is already made.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בריה דרבא adds a condition to the ברייתא from step 13. The order of actions matters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The act of putting up the מזוזה has to happen on a doorway that is already a doorway. If the מזוזה was already sitting in the reed before the frame became a doorway, nobody did any act of placing it on a doorway. The rule תעשה ולא מן העשוי says the מצוה must be done as an act, not happen by itself from something already there.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They only taught this when', a phrase that limits an earlier teaching
'You shall make', and not from what is already made; the מצוה needs a real act

steps.whatToRemember: A מזוזה must be put onto a doorway that already exists. If it was in place before the doorway was set up, it is פסולה because of תעשה ולא מן העשוי.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule, that a מצוה object must be made or placed as an act, shows up in many places, such as ציצית and סוכה.

phrases.english: Rav Acha son of Rava said:
They taught this only when he set up [the frame]
and afterward cut [the tube] and placed it;
but if he cut and placed [it first]
and afterward set up [the frame], it is invalid,
[for it says] "you shall make," and not from what is already made.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁהֶעֱמִיד וּלְבַסּוֹף חָתַךְ וְהִנִּיחָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ברייתא in step 13 by requiring a certain order of actions
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The reed-tube method is valid only if the frame was set up before the מזוזה was placed. The reverse order is פסולה because of תעשה ולא מן העשוי.

steps.title: Broken entrances are exempt from מזוזה
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that פיתחי שימאי, broken or incomplete entrances, do not need a מזוזה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: These broken entrances are exempt from the מזוזה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new ruling: some doorways are not proper doorways and do not need a מזוזה. The גמרא will next ask what these doorways are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a real doorway needs a מזוזה. רבא says some openings lack what makes a doorway a doorway, so the obligation does not apply. He does not yet say what is missing.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Broken entrances', openings without a proper doorway form

phrases.english: And Rava said:
these broken entrances
are exempt from the mezuza.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא: הָנֵי פִּיתְחֵי שִׁימָאֵי פְּטוּרִין מִן הַמְּזוּזָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New ruling about which doorways are exempt
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Broken entrances (פיתחי שימאי) are exempt from מזוזה.

steps.title: What are broken entrances?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what exactly רבא meant by פיתחי שימאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are 'broken entrances'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a definition of the term רבא used. It is setting up the argument in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's ruling cannot be used until we know which doorways count as 'broken'. This question is about what the term means, not a challenge to רבא.

phrases.english: What are broken entrances?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the definition of the term in step 15
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which kind of doorway counts as פיתחי שימאי

steps.title: Two opinions: no roof, or no lintel
steps.stepSummary: רב ריחומי and אבא יוסי argue. One says broken entrances are ones with no roof; the other says they are ones with no lintel.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ריחומי and אבא יוסי argue about it. One says: they have no roof. And one says: they have no lintels.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 16 with two different definitions from two אמוראים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that something basic is missing, so it is not a real doorway. One thinks the missing piece is a roof over the area. The other thinks it is the beam across the top of the opening. The גמרא does not decide between them here.

keyTerms.meaning: Lintels, the beam across the top of a doorway

steps.whatToRemember: פיתחי שימאי are exempt from מזוזה. One opinion says these are openings with no roof; the other says they are openings with no lintel.

phrases.aramaic: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַב רִיחוּמִי וְאַבָּא יוֹסֵי,
phrases.english: Rav Richumi and Abba Yosei argue about it:
one says: those that have no roof;
and one says: those that have no lintels.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַב רִיחוּמִי וְאַבָּא יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 16
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Two definitions: an entrance with no roof, or an entrance with no lintel

steps.title: A portico is exempt from a מזוזה
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rules that an אכסדרה does not need a מזוזה because it has no doorposts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר שילא said in the name of רב חסדא: an אכסדרה is exempt from a מזוזה, because it has no doorposts.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ruling: an open porch-like structure, an אכסדרה, does not need a מזוזה. The reason given is that it has no doorposts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מזוזה goes on an entrance, and an entrance is defined by its doorposts. An אכסדרה is open on its front side, so it has no real doorway to put a מזוזה on.

keyTerms.meaning: A portico, a porch-like structure that is open on its front side

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר שֵׁילָא, אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: Rabba bar Sheila said that Rav Chisda said:
A portico is exempt from a mezuzah,
because it has no doorposts.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר שֵׁילָא, אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of which structures need a מזוזה, now moving to the אכסדרה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אכסדרה is פטור from מזוזה because it lacks doorposts.

steps.title: Would doorposts really make it obligated?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the reason: posts on a portico only hold up the ceiling, so why would they create an obligation?
steps.simpleTranslation: This implies that if it has doorposts, it is obligated? But those posts are made to strengthen the ceiling!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads רב חסדא's reason closely and finds a problem with what it implies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the reason is 'no doorposts', then posts should make it obligated. But posts in an אכסדרה are support pillars for the roof, not a doorway. So it seems they should not change anything.

keyTerms.meaning: Strengthening the ceiling, holding up the roof
This implies (introduces an inference from a statement)

phrases.english: This implies that if it has doorposts, it is obligated?
They are made only to strengthen the ceiling!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the implication of רב חסדא's reason.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason 'because it has no doorposts' in רב חסדא's ruling.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reason implies posts would create an obligation, but posts in a portico only support the roof and are not a doorway.

steps.title: Even with posts it is exempt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads רב חסדא: even if the אכסדרה has posts it is exempt, since they only support the ceiling.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he means: even if it has doorposts, it is exempt, because they are made only to strengthen the ceiling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by explaining what רב חסדא really meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא was not saying posts would create an obligation. He meant that an אכסדרה has no true doorposts at all, because whatever posts it has are only roof supports. So it is exempt either way.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means (a rereading of a statement)

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהּ פַּצִּימִין – פְּטוּרָה,
phrases.english: Even though it has doorposts, it is exempt,
because they are made only to strengthen the ceiling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא by rereading רב חסדא's words.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב חסדא seemed to say posts would make an אכסדרה obligated.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even with posts it is פטור, because the posts are only roof supports.

steps.title: אביי saw porticos at רבה's house without מזוזות
steps.stepSummary: אביי reports that רבה's porticos had posts but no מזוזות, showing רבה held the posts are only roof supports.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: I saw the porticos of the Master's house, which had doorposts but no מזוזות. He holds that they are made to strengthen the ceiling.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings support from what he saw: his teacher's porticos had posts and still had no מזוזה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This real-life practice matches the reading from the last step. רבה did not put up a מזוזה even though there were posts, so he too held that such posts only hold up the roof.

phrases.english: Abaye said: I saw them,
the porticos of the house of the Master,
phrases.notes: "The Master" here is רבה, אביי's teacher.

phrases.english: that they have doorposts
and they do not have mezuzot.
He holds: they are made to strengthen the ceiling.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: חֲזֵינָא לְהוּ לְאִיסְפְּלִידִי דְּבֵי מָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the conclusion that posts in a portico do not create an obligation.
steps.raayaObject: An אכסדרה with posts is still פטור.
steps.raayaSupportSource: אביי's eyewitness report of רבה's practice.

steps.title: A ברייתא says a portico needs a מזוזה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges from a ברייתא that lists an אכסדרה among places that need a מזוזה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: a gatehouse, a portico, and a balcony are obligated in a מזוזה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to say the exact opposite of רב חסדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא said an אכסדרה is exempt. This ברייתא clearly lists an אכסדרה as obligated, which is a direct contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: A gatehouse, the entry room at the gate of a courtyard

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
A gatehouse, a portico, and a balcony
are obligated in a mezuzah!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב חסדא's ruling from a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's ruling that an אכסדרה is פטור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא explicitly says an אכסדרה is חייב.

steps.title: The ברייתא means a study-hall portico
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is talking about the portico of a study hall.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about the portico of the study hall.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is talking about a special kind of portico, not a regular open one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A study-hall portico is closed on its sides, even though its walls do not reach the ceiling. Because it is more enclosed, it needs a מזוזה, while a regular open אכסדרה does not.

keyTerms.meaning: Of the study hall, of the house of learning

phrases.english: It refers to the portico of the study hall.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the ברייתא by limiting it to a specific type of portico.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case to a specific structure
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to obligate every אכסדרה.
steps.terutzMaskana: It only means the enclosed portico of a study hall.

steps.title: A study-hall portico is really a full room
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that a study-hall portico is like a proper room, so it is obvious that it needs a מזוזה and would not be called a portico.
steps.simpleTranslation: A study-hall portico is like a full-fledged room!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer it just gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a study-hall portico is closed in like a real room, it should simply count as a room. Then the ברייתא would have no reason to call it an אכסדרה, so the answer does not fit well.

phrases.english: A portico of the study hall
is like a full-fledged room!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַכְסַדְרָה דְּבֵי רַב כְּאִינְדְּרוֹנָא מְעַלַּיְיתָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תירוץ of step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the ברייתא means a study-hall portico.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Such a portico is really a room, so the ברייתא would not call it an אכסדרה.

steps.title: The ברייתא means a Roman portico
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is talking about a Roman portico, which is built with many windows.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about a Roman portico.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer: the ברייתא means a Roman-style portico, and that kind needs a מזוזה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A Roman portico sits in the middle. It is more open than a study-hall portico, so it is still called an אכסדרה. But it is enclosed enough, with window-filled walls, to need a מזוזה. A plain, fully open אכסדרה stays פטור, as רב חסדא said.
steps.whatToRemember: A plain open אכסדרה is פטור from מזוזה even if it has posts, since posts only hold the roof. The ברייתא that obligates an אכסדרה is talking about a Roman portico.

phrases.english: It refers to a Roman portico.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer with a new definition of the ברייתא's case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case to a different specific structure
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא meant a study-hall portico, which turned out to be a real room.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא means a Roman portico, which is still called an אכסדרה but needs a מזוזה.

steps.title: A בי הרזיקי needs two מזוזות
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rules that a בי הרזיקי requires two מזוזות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רחבה said in the name of רב יהודה: a בי הרזיקי needs two מזוזות.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ruling about a structure called a בי הרזיקי: it needs two מזוזות, not one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We do not yet know what a בי הרזיקי is. This ruling sets up the next question, where the גמרא asks for a definition.

keyTerms.meaning: A type of gatehouse structure (defined in the next steps)

phrases.english: Rachava said that Rav Yehuda said:
A bei harziki is obligated in two mezuzot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic in the list of structures and their מזוזה rules.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בי הרזיקי requires two מזוזות.

steps.title: What is a בי הרזיקי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what a בי הרזיקי is.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is a בי הרזיקי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a definition of the unfamiliar term, setting up the answer that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To understand why it needs two מזוזות, we first need to know what the structure looks like.

phrases.english: What is a bei harziki?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the term used in רב יהודה's ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The definition of a בי הרזיקי.

steps.title: A gatehouse between the courtyard and the houses
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא סבא, quoting רב, explains that it is a gatehouse that opens to a courtyard, with houses opening into the gatehouse.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא סבא said in the name of רב: it is a gatehouse that opens to a courtyard, and houses open into the gatehouse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question and defines the structure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The gatehouse has two kinds of entrances. One leads from the courtyard into the gatehouse, and another leads from the gatehouse into the houses. Each entrance needs its own מזוזה, which is why there are two.
steps.whatToRemember: A בי הרזיקי is a gatehouse between a courtyard and houses. It has two entrances, so it needs two מזוזות.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא סָבָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב:
phrases.english: Rav Pappa the Elder said in the name of Rav:
A gatehouse that opens to a courtyard,
and houses open into the gatehouse.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא סָבָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A gatehouse opening to a courtyard, with houses opening into it, so it has two entrances needing two מזוזות.

steps.title: A gatehouse that opens to a garden and to a small room
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records a dispute about a gatehouse that opens both to a garden and to a small room. רבי יוסי says it is judged like the small room. חכמים say it is judged like a gatehouse.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: a gatehouse that opens to a garden and to a small room. רבי יוסי says it is treated like the small room. The חכמים say it is treated like a gatehouse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about a gatehouse with two doorways, one to a garden and one to a small room. רבי יוסי and חכמים argue about how to classify it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A garden does not need a מזוזה, but a room that people live in does. This gatehouse touches both, so the question is which one it 'belongs' to. רבי יוסי links it to the room, which means it needs a מזוזה. חכמים treat it as just a gatehouse, which in this setting leans toward being exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: Garden, which does not need a מזוזה
A small room, which does need a מזוזה
It is judged like (has the same legal status as) ...

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
A gatehouse that opens to a garden and to a small room:
Rabbi Yosei says: it is judged like the small room,
and the Rabbis say: it is judged like a gatehouse.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: בֵּית שַׁעַר הַפָּתוּחַ לְגִינָּה וּלְקִיטוֹנִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defining a gatehouse with houses opening into it (בי הרזיקי), the גמרא brings another gatehouse case: one that opens to a garden and a small room.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי: the gatehouse is treated like the small room. חכמים: it is treated like a gatehouse.

steps.title: רב and שמואל: the doorway toward the house needs a מזוזה according to everyone
steps.stepSummary: רב and שמואל explain that both sides of the ברייתא agree the doorway leading from the garden toward the house needs a מזוזה, because it is the way into the house.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב and שמואל both say: for the doorway going from the garden to the house, everyone agrees it is obligated. Why? Because it is the way into the house.
steps.whatsHappening: רב and שמואל start explaining the ברייתא by telling us which doorway is NOT part of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The gatehouse has two doorways. According to רב and שמואל, the inner doorway, the one you walk through toward the house, is obligated even according to חכמים, since it is how you enter a home. This narrows the dispute to the other doorway, which comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees (literally: the whole world does not argue)
Obligated (here, to put up a מזוזה)

phrases.english: Rav and Shmuel, who both say:
from the garden to the house:
phrases.notes: This means the doorway between the gatehouse and the small room, the one you pass through coming in from the garden side.

phrases.english: everyone agrees that it is obligated.
What is the reason? It is the entrance of the house.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts explaining which doorway the ברייתא's dispute is about.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The doorway leading toward the house needs a מזוזה according to everyone.

steps.title: רב and שמואל: the argument is over the garden doorway
steps.stepSummary: According to רב and שמואל, the dispute is about the doorway from the house side out to the garden. רבי יוסי treats the small room as the main area, so this doorway needs a מזוזה. חכמים treat the garden as the main area, so it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where they disagree is the doorway from the house to the garden. One master holds that the small room is the main thing. The other master holds that the garden is the main thing.
steps.whatsHappening: רב and שמואל finish their explanation by placing the dispute on the outer doorway, the one to the garden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is which space defines the gatehouse. If the small room is the main area (רבי יוסי), the whole gatehouse serves a home, so even its garden doorway needs a מזוזה. If the garden is the main area (חכמים), the gatehouse serves the garden, so the garden doorway is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: The main thing, the space that defines the place

steps.whatToRemember: רב and שמואל: everyone obligates the doorway toward the house. The argument is only about the garden doorway, and it turns on whether the room or the garden is the main area.

phrases.english: When they disagree, it is from the house to the garden.
phrases.notes: This is the other doorway, the one between the gatehouse and the garden.

phrases.english: One master holds: the small room is the main thing,
and the other master holds: the garden is the main thing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב and שמואל's reading by showing where and why the תנאים argue.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute is over the garden doorway. רבי יוסי treats the room as main, so it is obligated. חכמים treat the garden as main, so it is exempt.

steps.title: רבה and רב יוסף: the garden doorway is exempt according to everyone
steps.stepSummary: רבה and רב יוסף give the opposite reading: everyone agrees the doorway from the house side out to the garden is exempt, because it is the entrance of the garden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה and רב יוסף both say: for the doorway going from the house to the garden, everyone agrees it is exempt. Why? It is the garden's doorway.
steps.whatsHappening: A second pair of אמוראים gives a different explanation of the ברייתא. They start by saying which doorway everyone agrees on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב and שמואל had said this garden doorway was the one in dispute. רבה and רב יוסף say there is no dispute about it: it opens to a garden, and a garden needs no מזוזה. So the argument must be about the other doorway.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two pairs. רב and שמואל say the house doorway is agreed (obligated). רבה and רב יוסף say the garden doorway is agreed (exempt). Each pair puts the dispute on the doorway the other pair treated as agreed.

phrases.english: Rabba and Rav Yosef, who both say:
from the house to the garden,
everyone agrees that it is exempt.
What is the reason? It is the doorway of the garden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reverse of רב and שמואל's reading.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The doorway to the garden is exempt according to everyone.

steps.title: רבה and רב יוסף: the argument is over the doorway toward the house
steps.stepSummary: According to רבה and רב יוסף, the dispute is about the doorway from the garden toward the house. רבי יוסי says it is the entrance of the house and needs a מזוזה. The view of חכמים begins with 'all of it...' and is finished on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where they disagree is the doorway from the garden to the house. One master holds that it is the entrance of the house. The other master holds that all of it...
steps.whatsHappening: רבה and רב יוסף place the dispute on the inner doorway, the one leading toward the house. The opinion of חכמים is cut off here and continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוסי, this doorway is how you enter the house, so it needs a מזוזה. חכמים seem to view the whole gatehouse as one unit tied to something else. Their full reasoning is finished on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: All of it (the whole structure); this sentence finishes in the next part
From the garden to the house, meaning the doorway leading into the small room

phrases.english: When they disagree, it is from the garden to the house.
One master holds: it is the entrance of the house,
phrases.notes: This is רבי יוסי, so this doorway would need a מזוזה.

phrases.english: and the other master holds: all of it...
phrases.notes: The sentence stops here and finishes on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the first half of רבה and רב יוסף's reading by placing the dispute on the doorway toward the house.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute is over the doorway toward the house. רבי יוסי says it is the entrance of the house and needs a מזוזה. The view of חכמים continues on the next amud.
